subject: Renewal negotiation: burst credits & soft overflow safeguards
messages:
From: Emma Walsh <emma@helios-analytics.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helios-analytics.com
Date: 2026-08-22T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal questions — dedicated pool + burst protections

Hi Mina,

We’re starting renewal conversations internally for our Redwood Dedicated cluster (current commit: 24 A100s). Procurement asked me to confirm options around burst behavior during peak windows. Specifically: can we buy a predictable monthly "burst allowance" so we avoid unpredictable on-demand bills during end-of-quarter surges, and what guarantees can you provide if we hit sustained high throughput?

High level asks:
- Option to pre-purchase monthly burst credits (flat fee, invoiced with reserved capacity)
- Failover behavior: if burst credits exhausted, do requests get throttled, queued, or moved to on-demand at pay-as-you-go rates?
- Any hard caps or 30-day notice policies for capacity reductions?

We have a renewal call next Wednesday (8/26). Can you send a short options matrix and rough pricing so procurement can prepare procurement language?

Thanks,
Emma Walsh
Head of Platform Engineering
Helios Analytics

Attachment: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Emma Walsh <emma@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — dedicated pool + burst protections

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Quick reply with three pragmatic paths we've been using with other customers; I'll attach a draft amendment and a cost model.

Option A — Predictable burst credits (recommended):
- Buy a monthly pool of burst credits (token-based) that sits alongside your reserved A100 pool.
- Credits are consumed before on-demand billing; unused credits do not roll forward (we can discuss a 1-2 month grace).
- When credits are exhausted, requests fall back to on-demand at a capped rate you pre-approve; we can set a per-token ceiling to prevent runaway charges.
- SLA: reserved pool throughput unchanged; burst paths are best-effort but we provide a soft-guarantee window (90th percentile latency target) when credits are available.

Option B — Soft overflow with notice:
- We allow automatic soft overflow to on-demand for short (<6 hours) windows with a buffer of free-prefetch tokens to reduce cold-start impact.
- For sustained overflow (>72 hours), we notify and propose a temporary reserved upsize or a negotiated buyout.

Option C — Hard cap (procurement-preferred):
- Hard cap on total throughput — once cap is hit, requests are queued or receive 429s depending on route policy.
- Lower operational risk for you, but higher chance of degraded UX during surges.

Attached: draft amendment with pricing tiers and a cost-model (estimates for 5k/10k/20k burst hours). Priyom and Rishi — added you for any technical clarifications or alternate routing policies.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- 2026-08-22-draft-amendment.pdf (draft contract language)
- cost-model-v3.xlsx (burst credit pricing scenarios)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-22T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — dedicated pool + burst protections

Emma — quick technical note to add color on how "soft overflow" behaves in the runtime:

- Burst credit path uses the same serving runtime; we maintain a hot KV cache for prefetched tokens to keep latency comparable to reserved.
- When burst credits are available we route to a "burst lane" that may select slightly lower-quantized model variants to preserve cost while keeping latency targets.
- If credits are exhausted and route allows on-demand fallback, traffic is routed to cloud on-demand instances that may introduce 20-50ms extra tail latency depending on region and instance type.
- For sustained high load, our autoscaling still respects your reserved capacity as primary — we will not reallocate reserved GPUs away from your pool without 30 days' notice.

I recommended the soft-guarantee language Mina used: a 90th percentile latency target for burst lane when credits are available, and a monetary cap on per-month on-demand spend that must be approved by Helios before billing above that.

If useful I can join the 8/26 call for a 10-minute technical walkthrough.

- Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: procurement@helios-analytics.com
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Emma Walsh <emma@helios-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal questions — dedicated pool + burst protections

Mina/Emma,

Procurement reviewed the draft amendment. A few clarifications we need before legal signs:
1) We prefer a pre-paid monthly burst bucket (Option A) but require a transparent overage policy — any usage that exceeds the pre-paid bucket must be capped at a monthly threshold (we propose $20k/mo) and routed to a single monthly invoice line item.
2) Hard cap is acceptable if Redwood guarantees a 30-day notice before any reduction to reserved capacity.
3) Please confirm whether unused burst credit refunds or credits carry a refund policy; if none, we want a 2-month credit rollover as a concession.

Also: please include redlined Procurement contact in the amendment and a sample invoice line showing the burst line item. We need these by EOD Monday to keep our renewal timeline.

Thanks,
Helios Procurement

Attachment: none
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T17:48:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed concession and next steps for Helios renewal

Team — recap and proposed negotiation stance:

Recap: Helios wants Option A (pre-paid monthly burst pool) with a $20k/mo overage cap and 2-month rollover. They also expect 30-day notice for any reserve reductions.

Proposed concessions (approve to push to legal):
- Offer a monthly pre-paid burst bucket priced per our mid-tier worksheet (see cost-model-v3.xlsx) with a 2-month rollover credit (only if customer renews for 12 months).
- Implement an automated billing cap: once per-month on-demand overage reaches $20k, traffic enters a soft-throttle mode and we send an alert to Helios and SE/AM. Further usage requires explicit email approval.
- Guarantee no involuntary reserved-capacity reductions without 30-day notice (internal policy already enforces this).
- Commercial: 10% discount on additional reserved GPU units if they commit to an annual upsell at renewal.

Next steps: Mina to incorporate these redlines into the draft amendment and send a redlined PDF + sample invoice to procurement by EOD Monday. Priyom to prepare two short talking points for the renewal call on 8/26 covering latency expectations and the billing cap mechanics. Rishi to validate rollback behavior for queued requests when soft-throttle engages.

If everyone agrees, I’ll approve these minor commercial concessions so legal can finalize quickly.

- Laura
Director, Account Strategy, Redwood Inference
